summary: Package root. Eagerly re-exports lightweight names (dtypes, errors, typespec data models, value classification) and lazily attaches expression, relation, DAG, pydata-ingress and capability-policy names via lazy_loader so no dataframe backend is imported at init. Also defines the table_schema() and datacontract() convenience constructors.
key_functions: table_schema(columns: dict[str,str], **metadata) -> TableSchema — build a TableSchema from a {name: type_string} mapping
datacontract(source) -> type[BaseDataContract] — compile a contract class from a TableSchema, Pydantic model, Frictionless dict/JSON path/string, simple dict, or an existing contract class
extension_points: lazy_loader.attach submod_attrs map: new top-level names are added to the submod_attrs dict and __all__
lifecycle_notes: Root __init__ last touched by 838a285b (shared schema declarations and adapter ownership); bd0f13de added Arrow ingestion export (from_arrow); 9f2848d8 added DecimalDtype export.
documentation_hooks: Quick-start / top-level API reference (import mountainash as ma)
Lazy-import behaviour and optional backend installation
Choosing between table_schema(), datacontract() and DataPackage for schema declarations
risks: Eager exports from typespec and core.dtypes mean those subpackages must remain import-light; adding a heavy import here defeats the lazy design.
datacontract() resolves str inputs either as a file path or JSON text based on Path.is_file(), which is an ambiguity for odd strings.
Import cycles: toplevel is imported back by core, typespec, validation and others (e.g. `from mountainash import ...`), so ordering of eager imports matters.

evidence.detail: __all__ and lazy_loader.attach submod_attrs define the public surface
datacontract() and table_schema() defined at module level
